# Closing the stale-entity tail — what was acquired, and what is genuinely dateless

*Generated by `py -3 code/1081_stale_tail_dated_facts.py doc`. Every date in `data/clean/entity_dated_public_facts.csv` is stated by the source named on its row, and `as_of_date_basis` names the field that states it. Cedar's own clock is `checked_date`, which 830's `NEVER` regex excludes by name and which `verify` refuses to let any `as_of_date` equal.*

## The three numbers

| measure | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| untouched over a year | 287 | **398** |
| no usable date at all | 373 | **148** |
| in no substantive Cedar row | 83 | **0** |
| *the union of the first two* | 660 | **546** |
| median days since change | 112 | 134 |
| p90 days | 3,627 | 1,365 |

Before is `docs/ENTITY_FRESHNESS.md` as generated 2026-09-02 before this workstream; that file is kept at `docs/ENTITY_FRESHNESS.md.bak_2026-09-02_pre_1081_stale_tail_dated_facts`.

**`untouched over a year` went UP, and that is the instrument working rather than a regression.** 287 was an undercount: an entity with no date at all could not be counted as stale, because there was nothing to compare against. 255 entities gained a first real date here and most of those dates are old, so they moved out of the invisible bucket and into the visible one. The figure that cannot move in that way is the union of the two, and it fell by 114. So did p90, by 2,262 days — the extreme tail is shorter.

## Three findings about the sources

**1. The ANCSA annual-report corpus does not reach the ANVC tail.** The brief said 358 audited AS 45.55.139 reports at `data/interim/ancsa_txt_v3/` carry dated financials for the stale Alaska Native village corporations. Measured: those 358 reports come from **41** corporations, and exactly **one** of the 95 tail ANVC / ANCSA-group entities is among them — Gwitchyaa Zhee, already dated 2024-12-31. AS 45.55.139 exempts the small village corporations, which is precisely the population in the tail. Re-mining the corpus would produce nothing.

**2. The one register that would date all 95 is behind a bot wall.** `www.commerce.alaska.gov/cbp/...` answers **HTTP 403 with a DataDome CAPTCHA** — to `robots.txt`, to the entity search and to the bulk `CorporationsDownload.CSV` — measured 2026-09-02. Every Alaska corporation has a stated registration date, status and biennial-report date there. State: **NOT_ACQUIRED, host refuses automation**, which is not `SOURCE_DOES_NOT_PUBLISH`. A human-driven or records-request route would close 95 entities from one file and is the highest-value acquisition left in this tail.

**3. ProPublica answers a zero-result search with HTTP 404.** Measured the same day: `q=alu+like` returns 200 with one organisation, `q=ahfachkee+school` returns 404, `q=school` returns 200. The 404 is a fact about the QUERY, not about the host, and the first run of the search route counted three of them as a host refusal and stopped after two rows. The cause of those three was ours: `urllib.parse.quote` defaults to `safe="/"`, so *Baca /Dlo'Ay Azhi Community School* produced a query string with a live slash in it.

## Why NCES cannot make a BIE school look fresh

CCD collection year Y is school year Y/Y+1 and its snapshot is the 1 October membership count date. The newest year NCES publishes for fips 59 is **2024**, so the newest possible CCD date is **2024-10-01** — outside the 365-day bar by construction. And the BIE reporting universe is **static**: the same 174 schools reported in every collection year 2008-2024, so "the most recent year this school reported" is one date shared by all of them. That is the shape 830 refuses as a build stamp, and this script's own `verify` refuses it too. There is one narrow exemption, `uniform_source_date = Y`, and it is available only to dates **outside** the staleness bar, so it can never make anything look recent. `selftest` proves it is not a loophole by injecting a declared-uniform date of *today* across 120 entities and asserting the check still fires.

What CCD does give a BIE school is a first substantive row: an NCES BIE school number, the operating LEA, enrolment, teacher FTE, open/closed status and a location. That is what took **in no substantive Cedar row from 83 to 0**.

## Three identifier traps found on the way

**`ncessch` is not a school id.** It is `leaid` (7 digits) glued to the school's own 5-digit number, and NCES re-issues the LEA half whenever a school's reporting agency changes — Ahfachkee is `590000700041` up to 2005 and `590009200041` after it, one school, two strings. Keying identity on it reported **132 of 142** BIE schools as *ambiguous, two or more NCES ids*, which is a statement about a join key and not about NCES. Keyed on the last five digits: 116 matched, 26 did not. `school_id` is not usable either — the same school is `00041` in some years and `5900041` in others.

**`GSA_MIGRATION` is not a UEI.** `fac_tribal_single_audits.auditee_uei` carries that literal string on rows migrated from the FAC's pre-UEI system, and **40 tail entities share it**. The ambiguity guard caught it only because it was shared; a sentinel held by a single entity would have keyed that entity to every migrated row in the federal tables. A shape test, `^[A-Z0-9]{12}$`, now runs ahead of the ambiguity test.

**A tier-B UEI is a name guess wearing an exact key.** The UEIs in `bie_uio_identifier_links.uei` come from a name match against the BIE roster; that file's own `tier_rationale` says *"Tier B: the identifier is not independently confirmed"*. Treating them as exact links is START_HERE trap 1 in its purest form. 98 of the 115 tail UEIs are in that state, and they now earn a date only where the transaction's own recipient name also matches the entity. That re-check removed 6 entities and **4,111 prime-contract rows** from the result — rows that would have dated an entity from another organisation's contract.

## The self-reference defect, fifth occurrence

830 reads every table in `data/clean`, including this one. So an entity this script dates leaves the tail — and on the next run the slice no longer contains it, its row is replaced away (a route owns and replaces its own rows), and it returns to `no usable date`. The measure would oscillate and every run would look like progress. 830 hit this shape three times on date COLUMNS and 1021 once on row PRESENCE; here it is the SLICE. `tail_slice` now re-admits every entity already carried in the output, so the working population is monotone and a re-run can correct a row but never withdraw one. Proven: two consecutive full runs produced byte-identical output.
